summary: Iteration 14 — Security hardening (2FA staff MFA + upload validation + password policy + security headers + MongoDB-backed rate limiter + pagination + N+1 query fixes) verified. New suite tests/test_iteration14_security_hardening.py — 28/28 PASSED in serial mode (-n 0) in 123s covering: (a) baseline login for all four roles with NO 2FA challenge (client/accountant/admin/super_admin land at correct dashboards); (b) all required security headers present on /api responses (X-Frame-Options, X-Content-Type-Options, Strict-Transport-Security, Referrer-Policy, Content-Security-Policy, Permissions-Policy, X-Request-ID); (c) password policy rejects <12 chars, common passwords, passwords containing the user's email-local, accepts a strong password AND revokes other refresh sessions on change (session A refresh returned 401 after session B changed the password); (d) upload validation rejects .exe with 415, .html with 415, empty file with 400, 26MB PDF with 413, accepts a normal PDF with 200 and owner can download; (e) full 2FA lifecycle on disposable accountant.c — enrol returns otpauth_uri + manual_secret, activate with a valid TOTP returns 10 recovery codes, login with 2FA on returns {two_factor_required, challenge} and NO access_token, wrong code → 401, correct code issues session, the same challenge cannot be replayed (401), the same TOTP step cannot be reused (401), a recovery code works exactly once then fails the second time, client login is unaffected, ADMIN and SUPER_ADMIN both 403 on /auth/2fa/disable regardless of password/code (role guard first), accountant CAN disable with password + valid code; (f) pagination on /api/cases and /api/audit-log honours limit + skip and returns disjoint pages. Frontend E2E smoke: accountant.a signs in via UI and lands on /work, /staff/security renders with data-testid=staff-security-panel + twofactor-panel + twofactor-start-btn all present, and all seven required security headers verified via page.request.get on /api/auth/2fa/status through the production URL (all present, X-Request-ID unique per request). Both middleware fixes the main agent flagged confirmed: rate limiter returns JSONResponse (429) not a 500, and the MongoDB-backed counter persists across the ingress. Cleanup: teardown fixture unset totp/recovery_code_hashes on every demo staff account; I also stripped a stray totp record found on clienta@example.com (secret_enc set from an earlier main-agent run, enabled=false so it never affected login) so the demo accounts are exactly as documented. Client A / Client B case+doc+message state untouched.

minor.issue: TestTwoFactor flakes under parallel workers because a sibling worker running tests/test_hardening_cors_ratelimit.py (which also uses accountant.c and exhausts login attempts) races with the 2FA class. Runs 28/28 green under -n 0. Non-regression — the same suite is fully green serially. Fix option: pin TestTwoFactor to a single class using pytest.mark.serial or move the CORS/ratelimit accountant.c login sweep to a dedicated user.

critical_code_review_comments: security.verify_code correctly uses per-step replay protection: the loop refuses last_step and, on success, the login endpoint atomically claims that step via update_one({id, last_step: prev}, {$set: last_step: step}) so a concurrent second use of the same code races into modified_count=0 → 401. Verified end-to-end.

security.consume_challenge inserts the jti unconditionally before any code check, so the challenge is single-use regardless of whether the code succeeds — a wrong-code attempt also burns the challenge. Verified by test_f (challenge replay after successful use returns 401). This means clients must fetch a fresh challenge for every attempt, which the frontend already does via AuthContext.verifyTwoFactor.
protections.RateLimitMiddleware returns JSONResponse(429) instead of raising HTTPException — the previous 500 regression the main agent hit is confirmed fixed.
protections.RateLimitMiddleware counts in db.api_rate_buckets (MongoDB) rather than process memory, so the 300/min ceiling holds across replicas — matches the main agent's design note.

server.disable_2fa checks the role guard BEFORE the password/code, so ADMIN/SUPER_ADMIN 403 with any inputs (verified by tests that send code='000000') — this is the correct order, since an incorrect code from a privileged user shouldn't leak whether the role is even allowed to disable.

server.change-password revokes all other refresh tokens via db.refresh_tokens.update_many({user_id, revoked_at: null}, {$set: {revoked_at: now}}). Verified: session A refresh returns 401 after session B changes the password.

protections.validate_upload does size check before content-type check, so an oversize file with a valid MIME still 413s (verified), and content-type parsing strips the '; charset=' suffix so 'text/csv; charset=utf-8' is accepted.

Cases and audit-log now accept limit+skip on GET; audit-log fetches limit+200 raw rows before test-case filtering to keep the page size honest after the include_test cull — that's a reasonable trade-off but if is_test rows dominate the returned page could still be short of `limit`; consider iterating the query in a loop until the requested page is filled.

server.consume_challenge and server.login_2fa correctly split roles: the recovery code path calls db.users.update_one($pull) which is idempotent under concurrent reuse (pulled.modified_count == 0 → 401) so a race between two workers using the same recovery code cannot both succeed. Nice.

One quality nit: server.upload_document reads the whole file into memory before validate_upload runs, so a 200MB adversarial upload still buffers 200MB before the 413. Consider a streaming size check that aborts the read once MAX_UPLOAD_BYTES is exceeded.
